items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed after the review by commit 307aab137386e4077741552d01a58dd827b6ff7e, which switches the candidate scan to keyset on id alone, removing the precision round-trip; commit 3fcf9223cd981b496ab11200fbf69cc3904ba179 adds a regression test for a same-timestamp cluster spanning the batch boundary.
items.description: The open-case candidate scan pages with a keyset cursor whose updated-at component round-trips through a JavaScript Date (millisecond precision) while the underlying column stores full microsecond precision. Rows whose timestamp falls between the truncated cursor value and the microsecond boundary match neither branch of the cursor's or-predicate, so a cluster of rows sharing one timestamp that spans the 500-row batch boundary silently loses its remainder — those cases vanish from the paged view and its total count on every request. Bulk inserts share one transaction-stable now(), making same-timestamp clusters realistic.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 9b6127647771de5f35468c3d97021b8aee854531: the dedicated probe was removed, the first real list request carries the include-filter-options flag with the options cached client-side, and later interactions send the flag disabled; commit 3fcf9223cd981b496ab11200fbf69cc3904ba179 pins a single-request-on-mount test.
items.description: Initial mount fires two list requests — a dedicated one-row probe that exists only to fetch filter options, plus the main list query. The server pays its dominant per-request costs (the relationship-authorization batch check over candidate ids and the full universe count) for both requests, and the probe's page row, count, and hydration work are computed and discarded. This doubles exactly the per-mount work the change exists to bound.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 9b6127647771de5f35468c3d97021b8aee854531, which adds a direction-to-aria-sort helper applied on both sortable columnheader spans; commit 3fcf9223cd981b496ab11200fbf69cc3904ba179 adds the regression test.
items.description: The two sortable column headers expose no aria-sort attribute — sort state is conveyed only by color and a static icon, so screen-reader users cannot tell which column is sorted or in which direction, in markup added specifically for screen-reader support. A sibling table in the same feature area already solves this with a helper that maps the sort direction onto the columnheader element's aria-sort value, and the columnheader element (not the inner button) is the valid placement.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 9b6127647771de5f35468c3d97021b8aee854531, which derives an is-recovering-out-of-range condition and gates both the live-region message and the empty-state branch on it; commit 3fcf9223cd981b496ab11200fbf69cc3904ba179 adds a test that the empty state is neither announced nor rendered during recovery.
items.description: When a refetch shrinks the result universe while the user sits on a page beyond the new last page, the empty page response paints before the page-reset effect fires: the polite live region announces the empty-list message even though page 1 has rows, the empty state replaces the table for the duration of the recovery refetch, and the pagination control unmounts, dropping keyboard focus from the just-clicked button. The empty-state branch and the announcement need gating on the out-of-range-recovery condition.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted; a dedicated drift-guard spec comparing the stubs against the owning services' populate/field contract was added in commit 3fcf9223cd981b496ab11200fbf69cc3904ba179 and fails if either copy drifts alone.
items.description: The integration-test stubs duplicate the owning services' page-slice queries byte-for-byte (same populate tree, same field list), and no test anywhere calls the real service methods — so consistency pins that rely on the stubs guard a copy: a one-sided edit to either the stub or the production query silently disarms the pin while staying green. The stubs' claimed equivalence to the production SQL was enforced by nothing.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 8e4190688949a8fc34ae0907472a11faee136aee, which binds the caught error and emits a structured warn log with the case id before returning null.
items.description: A bare catch around the row-projection step returns null and discards the error entirely, while the only log for dropped rows attributes them to a hard-delete race. That race never throws — a hard-deleted case is simply absent from the query result and handled by the missing-id path — so this catch can only ever trap a genuine projection bug, which would then be misdiagnosed in production with zero error detail.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 8e4190688949a8fc34ae0907472a11faee136aee, which removes the direct dependency entry and switches the type import to the ORM's own knex wrapper package.
items.description: The newly declared query-builder dependency is type-only — the sole use is a type import, while the runtime instance comes from the ORM's own wrapper package. When the ORM bumps its pinned version of that library, the package manager installs two copies and the standalone type pin silently diverges from the runtime. Importing the type from the ORM wrapper and dropping the direct dependency keeps the types provably matched to the runtime instance.
